summary: Albertus Bruining (1846–1919) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University (Dr.theol. c. 1866–1871) under Paul Deussen and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern, becoming Professor of Theology at Amsterdam in 1900.

Albertus Wilhelmus van den Hoek (1951–2001) worked in Indology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University (B.A. c. 1968–1970; M.A. c. 1970–1976 under Jan C. Heesterman), also studying under Louis Dumont in 1977. He headed Leiden University (1989–1992).
Albinas Rimka (1886–1944) worked in Indology and other fields. He taught economics at Vytautas Magnus University from 1923 to 1925 and at Vilnius University in 1940.

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Albion Moonlight Butters studied at UC Santa Cruz (B.A.), Harvard (MTS 1991–1993), and Columbia (Ph.D. 1997–2006 under Robert Thurman). He was an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Turku (2013–2020) and Editor for Khyentse Vision Project (2021).

Albrecht Hanisch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg by 2000, studying under Michael Hahn. He served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber (1825–1901) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Christian Lassen, Johann Gildemeister, and Adalbert Kuhn. He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 to 1901 and founded Indische Studien in 1850.

Albrecht Wezler (1938–2023) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme and served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004).

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs (2016). His posts include lecturer at Shan State Buddhist University, research fellow at SUTD, and Council Member of the Pali Text Society.

Aleksander Brückner (1856–1939) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Lviv, Berlin under August Leskien, and Vienna. He held academic posts at the University of Lviv (c. 1878–1881) and Frederick William University Berlin (c. 1881–1924).

Aleksander Dunin Borkowski (1811–1896) was an Indology scholar. He studied philology at Chernivtsi University (1827), attended the University of Lviv (c. 1827–1830), and studied under Peter von Bohlen at the University of Königsberg (c. 1831–1834).

Aleksandr Arnol'dovich Freiman (1879–1968) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg and Giessen. He held professorships at Saint Petersburg State University (1919; 1938–1950) and worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Aleksandr Gilferding (1831–1872) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University under Viktor Grigorovich, completing a master's dissertation in 1852–1853. He served in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and presided over the Russian Geographical Society (c. 1869–1872).

Aleksandr Ivanovich Aleksandrov (1861–1918) was a linguist. He studied at Kazan State University under Baudouin de Courtenay and Mikołaj Kruszewski, and at Tartu. He was Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Sanskrit at Kharkiv (1886) and Kazan State University (1888–1911).

Aleksandr Ivanovich Tomson (1864–1935) was a linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1882–1887) under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov and Theodor Korsch. From 1897 to 1932, he was ordinary Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Sanskrit at Odesa University.

Aleksandr Leonovič Grjunberg-Cvetinovič (1930–1995) specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Ivan Ivanovich Zarubin at Saint Petersburg State University and held posts at the Institute of Linguistic Studies and St. Petersburg University.

Aleksandr Lvovich Duvernois (1840–1886) was a linguist. He studied at Moscow State University from 1855 to 1866 under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov and served there as Professor of Comparative Linguistics from approximately 1869 to 1886.

Aleksandr Mervart (1884–1932) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (c. 1904–1907). He served as head and Keeper of the Indian Department at Kunstkamera (1913, 1924–1930) and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1924–1930).

Aleksandr Mikhailovich Osipov (1897–1969) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University (c. 1922–1926), taught at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1926–1935), and became chair of Indian History at Moscow State University in 1936.

Aleksandr Semënovič Zimin (1880–1942) was an Indology scholar who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov in 1920. He served as a Docent at the Leningrad Oriental Institute in 1934 and worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in 1937.

Aleksandr Vasil'yevich Popov (1855–1880) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kupiansk Theological Seminary between 1871 and 1875 and studied under Vincenz Scherzl from approximately 1874 to 1879.
